summary: A narrator recounts receiving a message from Wheeze, a fellow member of their group, saying Wilson has been detained in connection with a terrorism investigation, and that Zip has been taken too. The narrator, who had checked the encrypted messaging program's code, feels shaken and suspects Zip is a rat, while reflecting on Wilson as a harmless, goofy friend whose past trouble was minor, such as the pickle-display incident at a grocery store. The excerpt is from Book 14, part 5 of a fiction work.
one_line: Narrator learns through encrypted messages that friend Wilson has been detained in a terrorism investigation, and suspects Zip is a rat.
key_facts: The narrator had used a campus computer once when they forgot their power cord and never went back there again.
The student worker told the narrator that the campus budget did not cover the whole campus, leaving a handful of spots surveillance-free.
The narrator's messages to Wheeze used end-to-end encryption and an open source program that everyone on the Group vouched for.
The narrator checked the program's code line by line.
Wheeze wrote that Wilson was "detained in connection with a ter- rorism investigation."
The narrator responded with "wtf ! ?" and felt the news was a disaster they had predicted but could not prevent.
Wilson was described as a doofus and a friendly doofus whose biggest problem was wanting everyone to like him.
Wilson once accidentally bumped into a display of gourmet pickles at a fancy grocery store, causing $600 worth of pickles and broken glass to explode across the floor.
Wilson kept laughing while the store manager tried to impress on him how serious the damage was.
Wheeze wrote that Zip had been detained too.
The narrator typed "He's a rat" about Zip after first deleting an earlier attempt to write it.
Zip had crashed on a couch at Wheeze's house after a protest and had been living there ever since.
Zip was older than Wilson and was a more take-charge kind of guy.
Everybody loved Zip, according to the narrator.
